tutorsList.headline: Conversational Native Friend
tutorsList.name: Charles Lambert
tutorsList.bio:
Professional English coach and tutor with 8 years of experience helping learners of all levels develop practical, confident, and natural English communication skills. Holding a Master’s degree in Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL)*and a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, I combine structured language instruction with a modern, engaging, and practical approach to learning.

My teaching philosophy focuses on active output, particularly speaking and writing, enabling students to communicate clearly and confidently in real-world situations. Rather than relying solely on traditional textbooks, I use diverse, relevant topics and personalized lessons tailored to each learner’s goals, whether for professional development, travel, academic purposes, or everyday communication.

I believe consistency, motivation, and an enjoyable learning experience are essential to long-term progress. My goal is to make English learning engaging and effective while helping students build the confidence and skills they need to communicate naturally and fluently.

landingContent.heroQuote: “Você não precisa estudar mais. Você pode viver em inglês.”
landingContent.heroSubtext: Transforme sua rotina diária em prática real. Do café da manhã ao trabalho e descanso noturno. Sua vida. Seu inglês. Do seu jeito.
landingContent.philosophySubheading: Aprender inglês não precisa ser uma tarefa pesada de 2 horas em uma sala de aula após um longo dia de trabalho. Conectamos seu aprendizado com o que você já faz todos os dias.
landingContent.philosophyPillar1Desc: Cada momento do seu dia se torna uma oportunidade de aprendizado natural — sem sobrecarregar sua agenda.
landingContent.philosophyPillar2Desc: Foque apenas nas palavras e expressões essenciais para cada momento. Qualidade e contexto superam quantidade.
landingContent.philosophyPillar3Desc: Sessões individuais ao vivo no Google Meet combinadas com correções instantâneas de IA no seu diário.
landingContent.footerSlogan: Learn English by living your life!

videos.description:
Explore how to build healthy habits when it comes to making, growing, and maintaining friendships.

--

Friendships can change how we see and move through the world. They can boost our academic performance, help us deal with setbacks, and even improve our health. And the relationships we form in adolescence can shape our beliefs, values, and emotional growth. But making and maintaining friends isn’t always easy. Iseult Gillespie shares how to build healthy friendship habits.

Lesson by Iseult Gillespie, directed by Biljana Labović.

Do you think you may be outgrowing your friends? Have you ever found yourself becoming distant from someone you used to be friends with? Outgrowing friends can be a sign of you getting more mature, pursuing your own goals, improve your personal growth, and knowing what you’re looking for in a friend. While it’s definitely sad, it’s completely natural and can even be a good thing in the long run. To help you identify whether you've outgrown your friendship, we made this video just for you!

Boundaries Build Respect.

Setting boundaries isn’t about being cold, distant, or difficult. It’s about teaching people how to treat you—and teaching yourself what you truly deserve. In this video, we’re breaking down nine powerful boundaries that instantly make people respect you. These aren’t theoretical ideas or unrealistic tips. They’re everyday behaviors you can use in your conversations, your relationships, your workplace, and even your digital life.
You’ll learn why a simple “no” can change the entire dynamic, how protecting your time reshapes people’s expectations, and why walking away from disrespect is one of the strongest signals of self-worth. Each boundary is explained in a clear, relatable way so you can actually apply it to your own life—without guilt, stress, or overthinking.
If you’re ready to stop being overlooked, overworked, or taken for granted, this video might be the turning point you’ve been needing.

#everydayenglish ##WhatIEatInADay #FoodVocabulary  #englishpodcast #learnenglish 

 What Do You Eat in a Day? | Daily English Conversation for Food & Eating Habits
Learn real, simple English while talking about one of our favorite topics—food! In this episode, Anna and Ben take you through their daily meals, share their favorite foods (and a few they really don’t like!), and explore different eating habits from around the world. Whether you eat toast for breakfast or noodles for dinner, this is a fun way to practice useful vocabulary, listening, and speaking skills in English.
🎯 What You’ll Learn in This Episode:
✅ How to talk about what you eat in a day – breakfast, lunch, dinner & snacks
✅ Easy phrases to describe taste, food preferences & cooking habits
✅ Common food-related vocabulary like stir-fried, savory, spicy, and texture
✅ How to politely talk about foods you don’t like
✅ Different eating habits around the world: meals, timing, and culture
✅ A listening + speaking challenge to practice your English fluency!

 Sample Phrases You’ll Hear:
• “I usually eat toast with jam for breakfast.”
• “My favorite food is noodles—they’re spicy and soft.”
• “I like cooking at home because it’s healthier.”
• “I don’t like olives because the taste is too strong.”
• “We eat dinner late in my country—around 9 p.m.”
• “I drink green tea after dinner to relax.”

🎧 Listener Speaking Challenge (Try These 3 Questions!):
1. What do you usually eat for breakfast?
2. What’s your favorite food and why?
3. Do you like cooking at home or eating out?
Write your answers in the comments—or say them out loud while listening!
